How this connects: This pattern represents the normal workflow used in Capstone Project. For Final Presentation, identify the input or starting state, follow the main operation, then check the visible result, saved data, log message, test, or release output.

Prepare a short presentation: the problem, a live demonstration, the technical decisions and their reasons, the difficulties you hit, and what you would do differently.

The last part matters most. Knowing the weaknesses of your own work is the clearest evidence of judgement, and every experienced reviewer is listening for it.

Key points

  • Open with the problem, not the technology.
  • Demonstrate the app live; have a recording as a fallback.
  • Explain two or three decisions and why you made them.
  • Describe a genuine difficulty and how you resolved it.
  • Say what you would change with more time.
  • Keep it under ten minutes and rehearse it aloud.

Example

Deliverable: a rehearsed ten-minute presentation with a working demonstration and a recorded backup. Live demonstrations fail; the recording is what keeps a failure from ending the presentation.

Why this matters

This is the same structure as a job interview's project walkthrough, so the rehearsal is directly reusable.

questions.question: Which language does this course use for Android development?
questions.explanation: Kotlin has been Google's recommended language for Android since 2019.

questions.question: What is Kotlin's headline safety feature?
options: Null safety enforced by the type system
questions.explanation: The type system separates nullable from non-nullable types, catching null errors at compile time.

questions.question: Where do you find the reason an app crashed while running?
questions.explanation: Logcat shows runtime output including the stack trace of a crash.

questions.question: Which unit should be used for text size?
questions.explanation: sp scales with both density and the user's font size preference, which dp does not.

questions.question: What is the advantage of ViewBinding over findViewById?
options: It is type-safe, so a wrong id fails at compile time
It removes the need for ids
It is shorter to type only
questions.explanation: Binding classes are generated from the layout, so mismatches surface during compilation.

questions.question: Which callback pairs with onResume?
questions.explanation: onResume and onPause bracket the period in which the screen has focus.

questions.question: What should SharedPreferences be used for?
questions.explanation: It is a key-value store for primitives, not a database.

questions.question: What does Firebase primarily remove the need for?
options: Building and operating your own backend server
questions.explanation: It supplies hosted auth, storage, database and messaging services.

questions.question: Why is RecyclerView efficient for long lists?
options: It loads all rows at once
It recycles a small number of row views as you scroll
questions.explanation: Only visible rows plus a small buffer exist at any time, regardless of data size.

questions.question: When is a navigation drawer appropriate?
options: For five or more top-level destinations
questions.explanation: Drawers suit larger numbers of destinations that would not fit a bottom bar.

questions.question: What should happen to the login screen after a successful sign-in?
options: Be popped so back does not return to it
questions.explanation: popUpTo with inclusive removes it, so back from Home behaves sensibly.

questions.question: Why must Room write operations avoid the main thread?
options: Disk work blocks the UI, and Room throws to prevent it
questions.explanation: Room enforces this deliberately so slow writes cannot freeze the interface.

questions.question: What identifies a specific app installation for messaging?
questions.explanation: Messages are addressed to the registration token for that installation.

questions.question: Which failures are worth retrying automatically?
questions.explanation: Server-side and transient failures may succeed on retry; client errors will not.

questions.question: Which accuracy should an app request?
options: The coarsest that satisfies the feature
questions.explanation: Requesting more than needed increases refusals and battery cost.

questions.question: What does elevation on a card convey?
options: That the card sits above the background as a distinct surface
questions.explanation: Elevation communicates surface hierarchy, not decoration.

questions.question: What happens to permissions declared in the manifest?
options: They appear on the store listing and are reviewed
questions.explanation: Users and Play both see the declared permission set.

questions.question: What is the classic cause of an Android memory leak?
options: Holding an Activity context beyond its lifecycle
questions.explanation: A retained context keeps the whole view hierarchy alive.

questions.question: How many phone screenshots does Play require as a minimum?
questions.explanation: At least two phone screenshots are required for a listing.

questions.question: What do AI-generated layouts commonly ignore?
options: Touch target sizes and contrast requirements
questions.explanation: Generated designs optimise for appearance rather than platform accessibility rules.

lessons.title: 🧪 Portfolio Review
lessons.html:
Module 19: Assessments & GraduationAssessment

Portfolio Review

Complete this examination, then review every answer explanation to strengthen your weak areas.

questions.question: Why are the first freelance contracts hardest to win?
options: Platform visibility depends on ratings you do not yet have
questions.explanation: Ranking algorithms favour established profiles, creating a cold-start problem.

questions.question: Why does the course teach Kotlin before the user interface?
options: It matches the Play Store order
Interface code is Kotlin code, so the language comes first
questions.explanation: Layouts are wired up in Kotlin, so the language is a prerequisite rather than a parallel topic.

questions.question: What keyword declares a function in Kotlin?
questions.explanation: Kotlin uses fun to declare functions.

questions.question: What does a breakpoint do?
options: Pauses execution so you can inspect variables
questions.explanation: Breakpoints suspend the running app at a chosen line for inspection.

questions.question: How many direct children can a ScrollView have?
questions.explanation: A ScrollView takes a single child, which is usually a layout containing the rest.

questions.question: How many destinations suit a bottom navigation bar?
questions.explanation: Below three the bar is wasteful; above five the labels no longer fit comfortably.

questions.question: What is the recommended app structure for navigation?
options: A single activity hosting a graph of fragments
questions.explanation: Single-activity architecture is what the Navigation Component is designed around.

questions.question: Where should an image be stored?
options: As a byte array in Room
On disk, with its path stored in Room
questions.explanation: Large binaries bloat the database and slow every query; store the file and reference it.

questions.question: What should never be logged as an analytics event parameter?
options: Personal data such as an email address
questions.explanation: Personal data in analytics creates privacy and regulatory exposure.

questions.question: Where should an API token be sent?
questions.explanation: Headers are not logged in the way URLs are along the request path.

questions.question: How should an API key for Maps be protected?
options: Restricted by package name and signing certificate
questions.explanation: Restriction at the provider makes an extracted key useless elsewhere.

questions.question: What is an appropriate duration for most UI transitions?
questions.explanation: Short transitions read as responsive; longer ones become tedious with repetition.

questions.question: What should be assumed about code shipped in an APK?
options: It is signed and therefore private
It can be decompiled and read
questions.explanation: Anything in the package is recoverable, so it can hold no meaningful secret.

questions.question: What does publishing an Android App Bundle achieve?
options: Play serves only the code and resources each device needs
questions.explanation: Bundles let Play generate device-specific APKs, cutting download size.

questions.question: How long is the Play short description?
questions.explanation: The short description is capped at 80 characters and appears in search results.

lessons.title: 19.1 Certificate Requirements
lessons.html:
📖 Certificate Requirements
What you must complete to graduate from this programme.

Key Words & Meanings

Tap a word to open its definition.

Certificate Requirements

Certificate Requirements is the focus of this Assessments & Graduation lesson. It helps the learner implement, test, and explain this Android development skill in a working application.

competency

The demonstrated ability to apply knowledge and skill to a required standard.

rubric

A scoring guide describing assessment criteria and performance levels.

certificate

A credential confirming that stated completion requirements were met.

📱 Kotlin or Android pattern to study

Completion evidence
- Kotlin and Android assessments passed
- Required apps available for review
- Capstone evaluated against the rubric
- Portfolio links work
- Official learner name confirmed

How this connects: This pattern represents the normal workflow used in Assessments & Graduation. For Certificate Requirements, identify the input or starting state, follow the main operation, then check the visible result, saved data, log message, test, or release output.

The certificate records completion of the whole programme: the technical modules, the ten portfolio apps in Module 17, the capstone in Module 18, and the final assessment.

Lessons unlock in order, so working through the course as designed satisfies the requirements. Retakes are unlimited, so a failed assessment costs time rather than progress.

Key points

  • Complete all lessons in Modules 1–16.
  • Build the ten portfolio apps in Module 17.
  • Complete the capstone project in Module 18.
  • Pass the final Certificate assessment with 70% or higher.
  • Retakes are unlimited.
  • Keep every project's source and screenshots — they are your portfolio.

Example

The certificate appears in the player automatically once every requirement is met. Keep the ten apps and the capstone in a public repository; those are what an employer will ask to see, and they matter more than the certificate itself.

Why this matters

The projects, not the certificate, are what get you hired. The certificate confirms you finished; the repositories show what you can build.

questions.question: What must be done with every AI-suggested change?
questions.explanation: Suggestions are drafts, not verified code.

questions.question: What is scope creep?
options: Gradual accumulation of unagreed additions to the work
questions.explanation: Small requests compound until the project far exceeds what was priced.

questions.question: What is Android Studio?
questions.explanation: Android Studio is the official IDE for building Android applications.

questions.question: What is the index of the first element of an array?
questions.explanation: Kotlin arrays, like most languages, are zero-indexed.

questions.question: How should resource ids be named?
questions.explanation: Purpose-based names remain meaningful as the layout changes.

questions.question: What happens to a view with no constraints at runtime?
options: It appears at the top-left corner
questions.explanation: Unconstrained views default to position 0,0 when the layout is actually rendered.

questions.question: What is an explicit intent?
options: One that names the exact component to start
questions.explanation: Explicit intents name the target class, typically within your own app.

questions.question: Can you rely on onDestroy always running?
options: No, the process may be killed without it
questions.explanation: Android can terminate the process without calling onDestroy, so critical cleanup cannot depend on it.

questions.question: What should the UI read from in an offline-first app?
options: The local database, with the network refreshing it
questions.explanation: Rendering from local storage means the app works regardless of connectivity.

questions.question: What does Google Play require for apps handling user data?
options: A publicly reachable privacy policy URL
questions.explanation: A privacy policy URL is a submission requirement for such apps.

questions.question: What should be checked before designing around a third-party API?
options: Rate limits, pricing and terms of use
questions.explanation: These constraints shape whether the design is viable and affordable.

questions.question: Where must a sensor listener be unregistered?
questions.explanation: Leaving it registered continues delivering events and draining the battery.

questions.question: Which layout adapts best to varying screen sizes?
questions.explanation: Constraint-based sizing responds to available space rather than assuming it.

questions.question: Why should an app never store passwords itself?
options: Secure hashing, reset and verification are easy to implement insecurely
questions.explanation: Delegating to an auth provider avoids a well-known class of vulnerability.

questions.question: Where is the underlying cause of a wrapped exception usually found?
questions.explanation: Caused-by chains reveal the original exception beneath the wrapper.
